feed.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
feed.subtitle: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

entry.title: Federal immigration agent shoots and injures man in Austin, Texas
entry.summary: A federal immigration agent shot and injured a Venezuelan immigrant during an operation in Austin, Texas, officials said.

entry.title: Former UN Deputy Secretary General on the role of the UN in today's biggest conflicts
entry.summary: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with former United Nations Deputy Secretary General Mark Malloch-Brown about the relevance of the U.N.

entry.title: What to know as world leaders converge at the United Nations this week
entry.summary: United Nations head António Guterres returns to New York for his final U.N. General Assembly as diplomacy falters over wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, and the global body faces deep divisions.

entry.title: Morning news brief
entry.summary: World leaders gather in New York for U.N. General Assembly, Trump says his proposed D.C. arch will be "military complex," FAA rolls out AI-enhanced software to manage nation's skies.

entry.title: 'Crossing the Red Line' examines the Biden administration and Israel's war in Gaza
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Akbar Shahid Ahmed, author of "Crossing the Red Line: Biden, His Advisors, and Israel's War in Gaza"

entry.title: Diesel -- the fuel the U.S. economy runs on -- hits record high
entry.summary: Diesel prices continue setting records, now above $6.50 a gallon. That could mean higher prices not just for truckers, but for everyone.

entry.title: How a national farm leader is dealing with record diesel prices
entry.summary: John Boyd Jr., president of the National Black Farmers Association, says soaring diesel costs are deepening a farm crisis as farmers face sharply higher fuel costs in the middle of harvest season.

entry.title: Is produce from a home garden safer than store bought? 'It depends'
entry.summary: A record-breaking summer for foodborne illness prompted more consumers to grow produce at home. But experts say it's the farming practices, not size, that matters for food safety.

entry.title: Conflicts over Israel divide some American Jews for Yom Kippur
entry.summary: For many Jews, Yom Kippur is one of the holiest days of the year. But as internal conflicts over Israel divide some American Jews, some are staying away from synagogues and family gatherings.

entry.title: Hundreds vie for the chance to become the new voice of Boston's Logan Airport
entry.summary: Hundreds of people answered Boston's Logan Airport's open casting call to find an authentic local voice for announcements.
